entries.title: I Samuel 1:1
segments: Of Ramathaim-zophim; not the Ramah of Benjamin situated near Gibeah, a few miles north of Jerusalem.

Its position is uncertain.  Some suppose it to have been the place now called Soba, a short distance west of Jerusalem. 
 
  Mount Ephraim; this was probably a mountainous ridge that had its rise in Ephraim, and was continued south through Benjamin under the same name; for Ramathaim-zophim seems to have been south of the tribe of Ephraim. 
 
  An Ephrathite; Samuel was of Levitical descent, and belonged to the family of the Kohathites.  See the genealogy,

, where the name Shemuel is, in the original, the same as that here called Samuel; Eliel is equivalent to Elihu, and Toah is only another form of Tohu.  His father Elkanah is called an Ephrathite either because he resided in mount Ephraim, just as the Ephraimites themselves are sometimes called Ephrathites,
; or, as some think, from his having lived in Bethlehem Ephratah.

entries.title: I Samuel 1:2
segments: When a man so far departs from the original law of marriage as to have two wives, he may expect to have peculiar trials.

entries.title: I Samuel 1:3
segments: The Lord of hosts; this is the first mention in the Bible of Jehovah under this title.  See

.  It means, God of armies, or of the multitudes of heaven, and of the universe. 
 
  In Shiloh; where the tabernacle then was.  It lay in the tribe of Ephraim, among the hills a little east of the road leading northward from Jerusalem to Shechem. 
 
  Eli; he was then high-priest.

entries.title: I Samuel 1:4
segments: Portions; of the offering on which they were to feast.

entries.title: I Samuel 1:5
segments: A worthy portion; larger and better.

entries.title: I Samuel 1:6
segments: Her adversary; supposed to be Peninnah.
Designed and needless provocations increase the wickedness of the giver and the unhappiness of the receiver.

entries.title: I Samuel 1:8
segments: A just sense of our unworthiness as sinners, and of the numerous mercies which God bestows upon us, would cure us of discontent.

entries.title: I Samuel 1:9
segments: The temple; the tabernacle; the temple was not then built.

entries.title: I Samuel 1:10
segments: The best way to obtain relief from trouble is to go to God in humble, affectionate, believing prayer, spread out before him our wants, and beseech him for Christ's sake to bestow the blessings we need.

entries.title: I Samuel 1:11
segments:
Give him unto the Lord; to be employed all his life in the special service of Jehovah. 
 
  No razor came upon his head; he should be a Nazarite.

entries.title: I Samuel 1:16
segments:
Daughter of Belial; an abandoned wicked woman. 
 
  Spoken; prayed to the Lord.

entries.title: I Samuel 1:17
segments: Fidelity in giving reproof, meekness in receiving it, and readiness to correct mistakes, and also to receive correction, are traits of character in the worshippers of Jehovah which prepare them for the mutual reception of his blessings.

entries.title: I Samuel 1:18
segments:
Grace; favor. 
 
  No more sad; she cheerfully committed her case to the Lord, and expected that he would answer her prayers. 
 
Prayer often brings sweet peace to the soul, before the particular blessings prayed for are received.

entries.title: I Samuel 1:20
segments: Samuel; meaning, asked of God.  It appears from

, that he was a descendant of Korah.  Thus out of the family of one whom God so sorely punished with sudden death, he yet in his great mercy raised up in after-times the prophet Samuel and the sweet singer Heman. The descendants of the ungodly, warned by the fate, and turning from the sins of their fathers, may through the grace of God become signally holy, honored, and useful. 
 
Blessings obtained of God in answer to prayer should be promptly and gratefully acknowledged, and measures be taken to keep his goodness in perpetual remembrance.

entries.title: I Samuel 1:23
segments: A wise woman will, if consistent, nurse and train her own children. Even if it keep her for a time from public worship, and occasion many privations and cares, yet, in the health, character, and conduct of her well-trained children, she may expect, with the blessing of God, whose wise and good arrangement she has in this respect followed, a gracious and abundant reward.

entries.title: I Samuel 1:24
segments: One ephah; about thirty quarts.

entries.title: I Samuel 1:28
segments: No blessings are more dear, and none give greater comfort, than those which are gratefully received from, and heartily devoted to the Lord.
